verdict.rationale: Remote's authentication docs tell users to issue a separate token per integration so each can be scoped and revoked independently. It also documents an OAuth consent flow that exchanges grants for access tokens acting on behalf of consenting companies, so per-integration scoped credentials are a first-party capability. However, the evidence never describes the scope model, the granularity of permissions, or agent-specific credential issuance, so least-privilege depth is unproven. Missing for 10: documented scope/permission catalog, agent- or MCP-specific credential scoping, read-only vs write scope controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.
